questions.questionText: The train arrives ___ platform number 4.
questions.explanation: A specific point or location such as a platform takes 'at'.

questions.questionText: She was born ___ 12 March 1998.
questions.explanation: Dates and days take 'on'.
questions.shortcut: Date/day -> on; month/year -> in; clock time -> at.

questions.questionText: The meeting will begin ___ 10 a.m. sharp.
questions.explanation: Exact clock times take 'at'.

questions.questionText: My brother is very good ___ mathematics.
questions.explanation: The adjective 'good' takes 'at' when it refers to a skill.

questions.questionText: The shopkeeper divided the sweets ___ the four children equally.
questions.explanation: 'Among' is used for more than two persons or things.
questions.shortcut: Two -> between; three or more -> among.

questions.questionText: There is a strong friendship ___ Ravi and Karthik.
questions.explanation: 'Between' is used for two persons.

questions.questionText: He has been absent ___ Monday.
questions.explanation: 'Since' marks a starting point in time.

questions.questionText: The students have been preparing ___ three months.
questions.explanation: 'For' is used with a period of time.

questions.questionText: The cat jumped ___ the wall and ran away.
questions.explanation: Passing above and across an obstacle is expressed by 'over'.

questions.questionText: He is married ___ a doctor from Madurai.
questions.explanation: The verb 'married' (state) is followed by 'to'.

questions.questionText: I am fond ___ filter coffee.
questions.explanation: The adjective 'fond' takes 'of'.

questions.questionText: She is afraid ___ lizards.
questions.explanation: The adjective 'afraid' is always followed by 'of' (afraid of lizards). 'From', 'at' and 'by' do not collocate with it.

questions.questionText: The farmers were happy ___ the heavy rain.
questions.explanation: 'Happy about' a situation or news is the standard usage here.

questions.questionText: He is accused ___ stealing the bicycle.
questions.explanation: 'Accuse' is followed by 'of'.

questions.questionText: The minister congratulated the team ___ their victory.
questions.explanation: 'Congratulate' takes 'on'.

questions.questionText: She insisted ___ paying the bill herself.
questions.explanation: The verb 'insist' takes the preposition 'on' before a gerund: insist on paying. Other prepositions are not used with it.

questions.questionText: The old man is suffering ___ high blood pressure.
questions.explanation: 'Suffer' takes 'from' for an ailment.

questions.questionText: He prefers tea ___ coffee.
questions.explanation: 'Prefer' is followed by 'to', not 'than'.

questions.questionText: The bridge is ___ construction and will open next year.
questions.explanation: 'Under construction' is the fixed phrase.

questions.questionText: She is senior ___ me by two years.
questions.explanation: Adjectives like senior, junior, superior, inferior take 'to'.

questions.questionText: The Principal was angry ___ the students for their misbehaviour.
questions.explanation: Anger toward a person takes 'with' (at is used for a thing).
questions.shortcut: angry with a person; angry at a thing.

questions.questionText: The thief was caught ___ the act of breaking the lock.
questions.explanation: The idiom is 'caught in the act'.

questions.questionText: He is tired ___ waiting for the bus.
questions.explanation: 'Tired of' means fed up with doing something.

questions.questionText: The new law is applicable ___ all citizens.
questions.explanation: 'Applicable' is followed by 'to' (applicable to all citizens), never 'for' or 'on'.

questions.questionText: The company has been in business ___ 1985.
questions.explanation: A fixed starting year with the present perfect takes 'since'.

questions.questionText: I will finish this work ___ Friday at the latest.
questions.explanation: 'By' means not later than a deadline; 'till' would show continuous activity up to Friday.

questions.questionText: The shop remains open ___ 9 p.m. every day.
questions.explanation: 'Till' shows a situation continuing up to a time.

questions.questionText: The Himalayas lie ___ the north of India.
questions.explanation: A neighbouring region outside the boundary is described with 'to the north of'.
questions.shortcut: outside the area -> to the north of.

questions.questionText: Karnataka lies ___ the south of Maharashtra and is not part of it, so we say it lies ___ the south.
questions.explanation: Outside neighbours use 'to the south of'.

questions.questionText: She has no objection ___ your joining the team.
questions.explanation: The noun 'objection' takes 'to' (objection to your joining), even when a gerund follows. 'Against' is not used here.

questions.questionText: The teacher was pleased ___ the progress of her students.
questions.explanation: 'Pleased with' for a result or thing is standard; 'with' is used with progress.

questions.questionText: He died ___ cancer last year.
questions.explanation: 'Die of' is used with a disease (illness as cause).
questions.shortcut: die of disease; die from injury/overwork.

questions.questionText: The pilot was blamed ___ the accident.
questions.explanation: 'Blame somebody for something'.

questions.questionText: The Chief Guest was received ___ a bouquet.
questions.explanation: The instrument or manner of receiving is introduced by 'with'.

questions.questionText: She has a great aversion ___ crowded places.
questions.explanation: The noun 'aversion' is followed by 'to'.

questions.questionText: The jury differed ___ the verdict, so a retrial was ordered.
questions.explanation: 'Differ on' a matter (disagree about) is used here; 'differ from' compares things.
questions.shortcut: differ from = unlike; differ on/about = disagree.

questions.questionText: Her accent is quite different ___ her sister's.
questions.explanation: In standard Indian-English usage 'different' takes 'from'.

questions.questionText: The minister is the author ___ several bills on education.
questions.explanation: 'Author of' links a writer to the work: the author of several bills. 'By' would reverse the relationship.

questions.questionText: He was deprived ___ his inheritance by the court order.
questions.explanation: 'Deprive' is always followed by 'of': deprived of his inheritance. Similar patterns: robbed of, relieved of.

questions.questionText: The officer was entrusted ___ the responsibility of conducting the audit.
questions.explanation: Entrust somebody with something (or entrust something to somebody).

questions.questionText: The trustees are accountable ___ the shareholders for every rupee spent.
questions.explanation: Accountable to a person, for an action.

questions.questionText: The rebels were unwilling to comply ___ the ceasefire terms.
questions.explanation: 'Comply' takes 'with': comply with the terms. 'To' is used with 'conform' or 'adhere', not 'comply'.
